# Pickup summary and delivery activity — design contract

Design specification based on `interface.md` and the installed local HIG snapshot dated 2026-10-25. No web lookup, implementation, SDK validation, simulator, GUI, device or accessibility execution was performed. Examples below are proposed copy, not observed delivery events.

## Decisions and boundaries

The widget answers **“What pickup information can the household safely see?”** The Live Activity answers **“What is happening to the delivery I am following?”** Keep periodic pickup data separate from an 80-minute bounded delivery. Do not infer that a parcel is ready for pickup from the supplied address or delivery duration; the brief supplies no readiness event or current delivery stage.

Replace second-by-second widget refreshes with meaningful timeline entries and system-controlled refresh opportunities. Use the Live Activity for changed delivery events, without promising second-by-second network delivery. Replace the inline accessory’s Accept, Cancel and Details targets with one details destination. These choices follow [Widgets: updating and interactivity](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/widgets#Updating-widget-content).

A shared Apple HomeView Modular face is household-visible even when its data originates on one member’s iPhone. It uses a small-family widget, not a watch-face accessory. Keep personal recipient, street address and gate code out of every widget and Live Activity payload, preview, accessible label and deep-link URL. “Private Live Activity” means personal event selection and minimized content, not a guarantee that the Lock Screen is private. Details require authenticated app access. See [Widgets: Apple HomeView](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/widgets#Apple-HomeView), [Live Activities: best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/live-activities#Best-practices), and [Privacy: protecting data](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/privacy#Protecting-data).

## Widget: Household pickups

Configuration: choose a household and explicitly enable “Share pickup summary,” with explanation “Everyone viewing the shared face can see pickup counts and status.” Default shared publication is off. Select only parcels authorized for this household; private parcels do not contribute to counts. No shared configuration may enable recipient names, address, codes or item descriptions. A member’s personalized HomeView Home Screen remains distinct from the single shared Modular face; this product deliberately uses the same safe summary on both.

| Surface / family | Content in priority order | Activation |
|---|---|---|
| iPhone Home Screen / system small | “Household pickups”; large “1 ready” only after verified readiness; freshness line | Open selected household pickup list |
| HomeView Modular / system small | Same summary; larger count/status, removable background, no secondary controls | Open safe household pickup summary in the supported app context; private detail requires personal authenticated continuation |
| iPhone Lock Screen / accessory rectangular | “Pickups · 1 ready”; “Updated 2 min ago” | Open household pickup list after system access requirements |
| iPhone Lock Screen / accessory inline | “Pickups: 1 ready” when fresh; “Pickups: update needed” when stale | One target to the same pickup list; no simulated buttons |
| Optional watch glance / accessory rectangular in Smart Stack | “Pickups”; count/status; short freshness line | Corresponding pickup list in a watch app if supplied; defer this widget variant until that destination exists |

No watch-face complication is proposed; a future face placement requires its own Complications route. The delivery Live Activity can already provide a paired-watch Smart Stack glance as specified below. Supported family/context decisions come from [Widgets: anatomy and platform considerations](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/widgets#Anatomy); watch responsibility follows [Designing for watchOS](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/designing-for-watchos#Best-practices).

**Concrete supplied-data rendering:** no pickup readiness is known. Show:

> Household pickups  
> Status unavailable  
> Last update 35 min ago

If an actual prior snapshot contains a ready count, stale rendering instead reads “Last known: 1 ready” and “Updated 35 min ago · Check in app.” Never manufacture that count from the supplied parcel. At the largest text size, retain “Update needed” and the single app destination before optional headings or decoration.

Fresh ready example: “Household pickups / 1 ready / Updated 2 min ago.” Verified empty example: “No pickups ready / Updated 2 min ago”; unavailable data must never become a zero count. Gallery description: “Check household pickups.” Gallery previews use labeled simulated safe data, including the stale variant. Initial placeholder retains the title with placeholder blocks; prolonged absence becomes “Pickup status unavailable.”

## Freshness and connectivity contract

The following thresholds are **product decisions**, not Apple requirements: pickup data becomes stale after 15 minutes; active-delivery data after 5 minutes, or earlier when the server’s validity ends. Store source timestamp separately from fetch timestamp. A cache read or failed refresh never resets source age. Reject older event revisions; reject implausible future timestamps as unavailable until reconciled.

| Condition | Widget | Live Activity | Recovery |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fresh valid data | Verified count/status and source age | Verified stage and valid arrival window | Apply newer authoritative revisions only |
| Refresh in progress | Keep last known content and original age | Keep current content while validity holds | No blanking or fake progress |
| Stale, connection unknown | “Last known…” plus age; inline “Update needed” | “Update delayed”; last confirmed stage and age; hide ETA | Request update when allowed; open exact app context |
| Connection failure actually observed | “Offline · Last update 35 min ago” with last known state if any | “Offline · Update delayed”; source age; no ETA | App offers Retry; restore freshness only after successful authoritative update |
| No usable cached data | “Pickup status unavailable” | “Delivery status unavailable” | Open app; explain failure and retry there |
| Signed out / revoked membership | “Open app to set up pickups”; clear household cache | End associated activity and remove private local event association | Authenticate and recheck authorization; never reveal cached household data |
| Sharing disabled / no household selected | “Choose a household in the app”; no counts | No effect on separately authorized personal delivery | Explicit setup in app |

Age alone does not prove offline. With the supplied 35-minute update and no connectivity evidence, use **stale**, not “Offline.” Retain the last successful snapshot during errors. Schedule a stale-state timeline entry at expiry and request reloads on meaningful server changes; actual widget execution is system-controlled. Always show source age or “Last known” where delayed reload could otherwise imply freshness. System date presentation may update the age without network polling. On app entry, revalidate and expose Retry if needed. See [Widgets: updating content](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/widgets#Updating-widget-content).

## Private bounded delivery Live Activity

Start from the authenticated delivery detail when the person chooses “Follow delivery,” once an active event is confirmed; explain that safe delivery status can appear on the Lock Screen and paired displays. Respect unavailable/disabled system capability with the same status in the app. Provide “Stop following” in delivery detail; this ends tracking without cancelling the delivery. Do not start from the 35-minute-old snapshot alone.

Event data: opaque delivery ID, monotonic revision, confirmed stage, source timestamp, validity deadline, optional arrival window, event start, and planned monitoring end. Shared pickup publication uses a separate authorization and sanitized model. Do not collect location, contacts, camera, microphone or HomeKit access for these glances; logistics status comes from existing authorized service data.

**Lifecycle:** not followed → confirmed active → followed → delivered / cancelled / failed / monitoring expired → ended. Freshness is an independent state while followed. Example confirmed stages are “Preparing,” “On the way,” and “Arriving”; they change only on server evidence. Do not draw an elapsed-time percentage as physical delivery progress. The supplied 80 minutes is the planned event duration, not an arrival guarantee. At start + 80 minutes without terminal confirmation, end with “Tracking window ended · Open app for latest status,” never “Delivered.” A new bounded follow session requires a new confirmed event window and explicit user action.

On confirmed delivery, cancellation or failure, end immediately. Keep a safe terminal Lock Screen summary for 15 minutes, then remove it; Dynamic Island and CarPlay remove the ended activity immediately. Stop following, sign-out and access revocation request immediate removal without retained summary. Request termination through server and local paths as available; expiry/ending while offline must be verified against actual SDK/runtime support and must not rely on app foreground execution. The UI must still mark updates stale if an end signal is delayed. Apple recommends clearly bounded activities, ideally no more than 8 hours, with immediate ending and a shorter useful retained summary; 80 minutes fits that design guidance. See [Live Activities: lifecycle](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/live-activities#Starting-updating-and-ending-a-Live-Activity).

| Presentation | Fresh example (simulated) | Stale/offline replacement |
|---|---|---|
| Compact Dynamic Island | Leading parcel + stage symbol; trailing “12–20m” only with valid server ETA | Leading parcel + warning symbol; trailing “Stale” or “Offline”; omit stage if needed for fit |
| Minimal, including multiple activities | Parcel + stage/check/warning glyph conveying current state, rather than logo alone | Parcel + warning; accessible description includes update delay |
| Expanded | Top leading parcel + “Delivery”; top trailing valid arrival window; below confirmed stage and source age | Same identity positions; “Update delayed” or “Offline”; “Last confirmed: On the way”; “Updated 35 min ago”; omit arrival window |
| Lock Screen | “Delivery”; prominent confirmed stage; valid arrival window; source age; one “Details” link | “Delivery / Update delayed / Updated 35 min ago / Details”; add last known stage only when known |

All taps, including both compact halves, resolve the opaque delivery ID to the same authenticated delivery detail, preserving context through interruption and sign-in. “Details” is the only action; Accept and Cancel remain inside authenticated detail after current-state validation. No cancellation or acceptance is queued silently while offline. Multiple deliveries retain independent opaque IDs; minimal presentations remain distinguishable by accessible event labels without exposing recipient/address.

Updates occur only for changed content, validity or lifecycle; no one-second polling, fake live spinner, or speculative countdown to delivery. Alert once for a confirmed crucial arrival/action-needed event, subject to user/system settings; do not issue a duplicate push. Staleness alone is a quiet status change. [Live Activities: presentation and interactivity](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/live-activities#Presentation).

## Appearance, privacy and continuation

Use semantic system text styles: headline for status, body for detail, caption for freshness, medium/semibold for essential Live Activity text. Use actual text and scalable symbols. Stack source age beneath status, remove optional heading/detail before essential state, and grow expanded/Lock Screen content within system constraints. Keep fixed-family widget layouts flexible instead of assuming one production canvas. Preserve core stale/unknown wording through long text, Bold Text and large text. [Typography: Dynamic Type](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/typography#Supporting-Dynamic-Type).

Full color: semantic foreground/background. Accented: primary group holds state and freshness; accent group holds only supporting parcel identity. Vibrant: opaque grayscale values preserve hierarchy. Test light/dark, tinted/clear and removed backgrounds. HomeView Modular and StandBy use background removal and readable large summaries; red monochrome Night Mode retains written stale state. Do not use color alone for ready/offline/stale. Only Lock Screen Live Activity gets a restrained custom background; Dynamic Island backgrounds remain system-owned. See [Widgets: rendering modes](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/widgets#Rendering-modes) and [Live Activities: colors](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/live-activities#Choosing-colors).

Always On pairs: active shows status, freshness and Details; dimmed preserves positions and safe status, reduces secondary emphasis, and does not animate. No names, address or code appear in either. Resume preserves selected event. Respect system privacy redaction, using “Delivery update / Open app for details” if needed. Always On support depends on hardware/OS; the local guide’s specific device examples are not a complete current support list. [Always On](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/always-on#Best-practices).

Paired watch Live Activity: use default Smart Stack composition with stage/valid arrival window or “Update delayed”; tap opens watch detail if available, otherwise system full-screen continuation with paired-iPhone launch. No independent watch app is assumed. StandBy uses the safe Lock Screen layout scaled for distance and red-mode legibility. CarPlay shows readable status without depending on buttons/toggles, which are disabled there. Paired Mac activation follows system iPhone Mirroring. Do not promise Live Activity support on HomeView, tvOS or visionOS from this guide; HomeView receives the summary widget. [Live Activities: destination qualifications](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/live-activities#Platform-considerations).

Privacy data-purpose matrix:

| Data | Purpose / location | Access policy |
|---|---|---|
| Household authorized pickup count and timestamp | Shared glance, sanitized widget cache | Explicit sharing selection; exclude private parcels; purge on revocation |
| Delivery stage, timestamp, valid arrival window | Personal bounded activity | Followed event only; safe even when externally visible |
| Recipient and street address | Identify destination in app | Authenticated authorized detail only |
| Gate code | Entry instruction in app | Authenticated explicit reveal; encrypted secret storage where cached; never surface payload or URL |

This minimizes exposure; it does not certify security. Shared caches and already-rendered snapshots may persist until system refresh/removal. Revocation propagation and secure cache deletion require implementation evidence. [Privacy: best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/privacy#Best-practices).

## Acceptance checks and evidence status

**Passed — specification inspection only:** supplied 35-minute snapshot is explicitly stale; unknown readiness stays unknown; no unsupported one-second widget promise; shared/public surface content excludes recipient/address/code; inline has one destination; delivery has a bounded lifecycle and terminal behavior; compact/minimal/expanded/Lock Screen and paired-watch contracts exist. The commands read the installed root, selected families, topic procedures and local references; no external sources were fetched.

**Failed — supplied proposal:** full address/code on shared face exposes private information; one-second widget refresh promises continuous behavior the widget contract cannot guarantee; independent Accept/Cancel/Details inline targets conflict with its single target. These are brief-level findings, not observed runtime failures. The replacement specification resolves them on paper.

**Not executed — implementation acceptance gates:**

| Check | Expected observable result / missing evidence |
|---|---|
| 35-minute snapshot, refresh failure and recovery | Stale visible; age unchanged after cache read/failure; Offline only after observed failure; newer authoritative revision restores fresh state. Need state reducer fixtures and runtime evidence. |
| Expiry while backgrounded/offline | Widget retains honest source age; activity invalidates ETA and ends bounded monitoring; delayed push cannot resurrect terminal event. Need SDK-supported lifecycle design and timed disconnected-device run. |
| Completion and opt-out | End immediately; 15-minute summary only for terminal outcomes; Stop following never cancels delivery. Need server events and actual activity dismissal observations. |
| Routing/auth | Each target opens correct household/event; sign-in preserves destination; revoked user cannot view old detail; no secret in URLs. Need implemented routes and authorization tests. |
| Privacy | Shared face, gallery, dimmed screen, accessible labels and paired surfaces contain no private fields; sharing/revocation reflected. Need payload/cache inspection and multi-account household-device tests. |
| Rendering | Status/freshness readable in light/dark, accent, clear, vibrant, background removal, Night Mode and Always On; Dynamic Island limited-width layout fits without lost warning. Need native previews/screenshots and physical viewing checks. |
| Text and access | Check supported Dynamic Type sizes through AX5 on iPhone widgets, at least 200% text on iPhone and 140% on watch per local guidance; long/localized labels preserve essential status. VoiceOver announces status then freshness then destination; no secret labels. Need actual native text layouts, VoiceOver and assistive input execution. |
| Contrast and activation | Measure actual foreground/background pairs; use iOS/watchOS 44 × 44 pt default control areas where app controls are provided; system accessory targets use native family behavior. Need measured contrast/geometry, Increase Contrast checks and device usability. |
| Alerts / competing activities | One crucial event produces one alert; no duplicate push; minimal state communicates current status with other activities present. Need push logs and multi-activity device run. |

Accessibility values are scoped guidance from [Accessibility: vision and mobility](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/accessibility#Vision), not evidence of conformance. No runtime checks are claimed passed.

Still missing: actual pickup readiness and confirmed delivery stage; backend freshness/ETA guarantees and event timestamps; meaning of Accept and cancellation rules; household membership and sharing authorization model; supported OS/hardware/SDK versions; whether watch app and HomeView app continuation exist; secure storage and revocation behavior; all native renderings, measurements and execution above. The 15/5-minute freshness thresholds and 80-minute monitoring cutoff require product/backend approval before implementation. Local snapshot source links document rationale; current API availability remains unverified under the local-only constraint.

# Pickup summary and delivery activity

Design specification based on `interface.md` and the installed local Apple HIG snapshot. No web research, implementation, SDK compilation, GUI, device, or accessibility execution was performed. Example copy below is simulated; the brief supplies a parcel and a 35-minute-old update, but does not establish pickup readiness or a current ETA.

## Concrete result

The household glance answers **“Is there a pickup to check?”** The personal Live Activity answers **“What is happening with the delivery I’m following?”** They have separate content payloads and lifecycles.

### Household pickup widget

Choose a **system-small** widget for iPhone Home Screen and the shared Apple HomeView Modular face. This is a supported combination in the supplied snapshot; do not substitute a Lock Screen accessory family on the Modular face. Gallery title: “Household pickups”; description: “Check your household pickup summary.”

Small layout, in reading order:

```text
[parcel symbol] Household pickups
Pickup status unknown
Updated 35 min ago
Open app to check
```

After fresh, confirmed readiness, example content becomes “1 pickup ready” and “Updated just now.” A confirmed empty result reads “No pickups ready.” Never derive readiness from the presence of a parcel. Multiple authorized parcels aggregate into a count; the widget does not enumerate people or locations. The primary state occupies the largest text, with freshness directly beneath it. Use flexible system styles and margins rather than a fixed production canvas.

| Destination | Family and content | Activation |
|---|---|---|
| iPhone Home Screen | System small; same household-safe summary | Opens household pickup list, preserving household selection |
| Shared HomeView Modular face | System small; large primary status, short freshness line; removable background | Opens safe summary through the supported host route; personal details require the authorized personal app session |
| iPhone Lock Screen | Accessory inline: “Pickups · status unknown” when stale; fresh example “1 pickup ready” | One target to pickup list; freshness is the first detail there |
| iPhone Lock Screen | Accessory rectangular: “Pickup status unknown” / “Updated 35 min ago” | One target to pickup list |
| Paired Watch | Use delivery Live Activity in Smart Stack for this bounded event | Native system route described below; no separate watch complication in this design |

Remove the proposed inline Accept, Cancel and Details targets. Inline has one tap target; render a single summary, with no button-like subdivisions. Accept/Cancel, if the backend supports these operations, belong in the authorized parcel detail flow after current status is obtained. A tap never implicitly accepts or cancels anything. [Widgets: interactivity and supported families](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/widgets#Adding-interactivity).

### Privacy and configuration

Default household configuration is “Not sharing pickups / Set up in app.” The account holder chooses an authorized household and explicitly enables **“Share pickup summary”**, with explanation: “People in your household can see pickup counts and status. Names, addresses and access codes stay private.” This is a product sharing choice, not a fabricated OS permission alert. Until configured, expose no parcel existence or count. Personalized HomeView Home Screens still use the safe payload; the shared Modular face must never inherit private preferences.

| Data | Purpose and exposure |
|---|---|
| Authorized aggregate readiness/count and server timestamp | Household summary, only after sharing is enabled |
| Recipient name and full street address from the brief | Personal parcel detail after authorization; omitted from widget and activity payloads, previews, labels, and public caches |
| Gate/access code from the brief | Reveal only deliberately in the authorized app detail flow; store with established protected mechanisms, never in widget/activity snapshots or deep-link parameters |
| Opaque parcel ID | Personal activity routing; app checks account authorization on every entry |
| Device location, contacts, camera | No dependency for these glances; request no new access |

The Live Activity is personal to the followed delivery, **not a confidential screen**: Lock Screen, paired devices and across-room presentations can expose it. Even unlocked presentations use “Delivery” and a nonsecret icon rather than name/address/code. A “Hide delivery status” app setting reduces exposed content to “Delivery active / Open app”; it also applies to cached presentations. Revoking sharing/signing out clears local shared data and requests replacement with “Set up in app”; do not promise instantaneous remote cache erasure. Purge requests and propagation require verification. These are deliberate product privacy choices grounded in [Privacy: data minimization and protection](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/privacy#Best-practices) and [Widgets: Apple HomeView](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/widgets#Apple-HomeView).

### Private bounded delivery Live Activity

An **80-minute** delivery is a bounded frequently changing event suited to a Live Activity; it is not a reason to reload a widget every second. Start after the person chooses “Follow delivery” on an authorized active delivery. Explain where status can appear and provide “Stop following” in that delivery view. If activities are unavailable/disabled, keep the same status in the app without blocking delivery. Do not start from a stale cached state as though the event is confirmed active. [Live Activities: best practices and lifecycle](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/live-activities#Best-practices).

| Presentation | Fresh, confirmed in-transit example | Stale/offline replacement |
|---|---|---|
| Compact | Leading parcel glyph; trailing “20 min” only with a valid estimate | Parcel with warning glyph; “Stale”; no expired countdown |
| Minimal / multiple activities | Parcel plus changing remaining-minutes value when space permits | Parcel plus warning mark; accessible meaning “Delivery status out of date”; never logo alone |
| Expanded | Parcel upper leading, “Delivery”; status/ETA in consistent relative position; update age beneath | “Status out of date”; “Last confirmed: in transit”; “Updated 35 min ago” |
| Lock Screen | Same hierarchy, distinct task banner; optional supported Lock Screen background only | Same stale copy plus “Offline” only when positively known; one “Open delivery” link |
| StandBy | Enlarged safe status/ETA; secondary age; adequate margins | Large “Status out of date”; no misleading timer; red Night Mode preserves meaning |
| Watch Smart Stack | Default compact-halves composition, shortened status; no action dependency | Warning + stale status; full freshness on opening |
| CarPlay projection | Read-only compact status, useful without controls | Warning + stale status; controls disabled by platform |
| Paired Mac | Compact/minimal/expanded safe content | Same stale policy; activation uses iPhone Mirroring |

Both compact halves and all other app links resolve to the same opaque delivery ID. With no Watch app assumed, Watch tap opens the system full-screen activity with paired-iPhone launch button; do not promise an installed Watch app. HomeView receives the widget, not a newly invented Live Activity destination. tvOS/visionOS Live Activities are excluded by the snapshot. Preserve app context across interruption, rotation, authentication and return. [Live Activities: presentations and platform considerations](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/live-activities#Presentation), [iOS conventions](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/designing-for-ios#Best-practices), [watchOS glances](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/designing-for-watchos#Best-practices).

No direct delivery-changing action is needed on the activity. “Open delivery” is the sole essential path; stopping tracking in the app never cancels delivery. Do not add promotional content.

## Freshness and event contract

The following thresholds are **product proposals**, not Apple refresh guarantees: household summary fresh for 15 minutes; active delivery fresh for 5 minutes after its last authoritative event. Use server `updatedAt`, a monotonic event version, confirmed phase, optional estimate with validity deadline, and event ID. Reject older versions; future/invalid timestamps yield unknown freshness. Keep transport connectivity separate from server age.

| Condition | Widget | Live Activity / transition |
|---|---|---|
| No cached data | “Pickup status unavailable / Open app to check”; no invented count | No start until confirmed active; existing activity shows “Status unavailable” |
| Fresh authoritative result | Count/readiness and update age | Confirmed phase; ETA only while valid; phase changes only from authoritative events |
| Refresh pending | Keep last useful summary and age | Keep confirmed phase; freshness clock continues; no full replacement spinner |
| Beyond freshness deadline | “Pickup status unknown / Updated … ago” | “Status out of date”; mark last phase as last confirmed, suppress expired ETA |
| Positively known offline | Add “Offline” where space permits, retaining age | “Offline · updated … ago”; no assertion that courier stopped |
| Old data but network unknown | Say stale/unknown, never infer offline | Same; reconnect alone does not make data fresh |
| Reconnect + newer valid event | Restore confirmed state after response | Restore phase/ETA only after accepted update; no fabricated progress during outage |
| Signed out / revoked / no authorization | “Set up in app”; clear cached count | End activity and clear personal caches; app route authenticates or explains unavailable access |
| Delivered / cancelled / failed terminal event | Reflect new aggregate on next system opportunity | End immediately; safe “Delivered”, “Delivery cancelled”, or “Delivery ended” summary retained for 15 minutes where allowed, then removed |
| 80-minute expected end reached without terminal evidence | Remain truthful about unknown pickup state | End tracking with “Tracking ended · check delivery”; never infer delivered |

The 80-minute expected end is a proposed tracking deadline from confirmed start. A newer authoritative delay may extend it with a new explicit bounded deadline, up to a product cap of 2 hours total; at that cap, end tracking as unconfirmed and leave the app available. Stopping following ends immediately with no retained summary. Once ended, ignore late nonterminal events for that activity; obtain current state before offering a new follow session. Apple guidance favors bounded events ideally no more than 8 hours; the 2-hour cap is our shorter product decision, not a platform limit.

For the supplied **35-minute-old update**, both freshness thresholds have expired: show unknown/stale status, preserve age, do not assert readiness, arrival time, or offline connectivity.

Request widget timeline entries at meaningful known boundaries (including freshness expiry), plus reload opportunities after accepted data changes. System scheduling controls actual delivery; no per-second polling or visible-update guarantee. Use system time presentation for age when supported. Deliver changed Live Activity content from the authoritative event channel; schedule stale/ending handling through supported lifecycle mechanisms to be validated against SDKs. A ticking estimate is not evidence of server updates. If platform scheduling cannot guarantee a transition on time, expire ETA validity and use conservative snapshot wording rather than promise exact execution. Alert only for a verified crucial event such as arrival; deduplicate by event ID with notification channels so there is no parallel push for the same update. [Widget updating](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/widgets#Updating-widget-content), [Activity ending and update policy](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/live-activities#Starting-updating-and-ending-a-Live-Activity).

## Rendering and accessibility decisions

Use actual text, system styles and semantic colors. State is always expressed in words and a symbol; color is supporting information. Full-color uses light/dark semantic treatment. Accented rendering keeps status primary and the parcel glyph accent; it must survive a single user tint and clear treatment. Vibrant rendering uses grayscale brightness for hierarchy, with opaque light primary text and darker secondary text, rather than opacity alone. HomeView/StandBy remove background; test Modular Night Mode red monochrome. Keep essential status before secondary age/detail when text enlarges; inline uses its deliberately shortened status, with full detail on opening. No text is shrunk to force multiple actions into an accessory. [Widgets: rendering modes and text](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/widgets#Rendering-modes).

Active and Always On layouts retain the same content positions. Dim secondary details and rest animations; no pulsing courier marker or continuously moving map. Safe status stays readable; secrets remain absent in both states. On supported devices, test reduced-luminance grayscale and dismissal-control contrast. Device support must be checked, not inferred for every iPhone from the older Always On reference. [Always On](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/always-on#Best-practices).

Acceptance targets include text enlargement of at least 200% on iPhone and 140% on Watch, appropriate system widget text-size support, no essential clipping, and a task path usable without sound, color or precise gestures. Prefer standard system links; give status meaningful accessible text and label warning state explicitly. App controls use the iOS 44 × 44 pt default target as the starting point, with adequate separation; this is not a reason to invent accessory subtargets. Measure actual foreground/background contrast using the local guide’s stated Accessibility Inspector guidance (up to 17 pt: 4.5:1; 18 pt or bold: 3:1), preserving its scope rather than claiming universal conformance. [Accessibility: vision and mobility](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/accessibility#Vision).

# Pickup summary and delivery activity — design contract

Design specification based on `interface.md` and the installed local HIG snapshot dated 2026-10-25. No web lookup, implementation, SDK validation, simulator, GUI, device or accessibility execution was performed. Examples below are proposed copy, not observed delivery events.

## Decisions and boundaries

The widget answers **“What pickup information can the household safely see?”** The Live Activity answers **“What is happening to the delivery I am following?”** Keep periodic pickup data separate from an 80-minute bounded delivery. Do not infer that a parcel is ready for pickup from the supplied address or delivery duration; the brief supplies no readiness event or current delivery stage.

Replace second-by-second widget refreshes with meaningful timeline entries and system-controlled refresh opportunities. Use the Live Activity for changed delivery events, without promising second-by-second network delivery. Replace the inline accessory’s Accept, Cancel and Details targets with one details destination. These choices follow [Widgets: updating and interactivity](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/widgets#Updating-widget-content).

A shared Apple HomeView Modular face is household-visible even when its data originates on one member’s iPhone. It uses a small-family widget, not a watch-face accessory. Keep personal recipient, street address and gate code out of every widget and Live Activity payload, preview, accessible label and deep-link URL. “Private Live Activity” means personal event selection and minimized content, not a guarantee that the Lock Screen is private. Details require authenticated app access. See [Widgets: Apple HomeView](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/widgets#Apple-HomeView), [Live Activities: best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/live-activities#Best-practices), and [Privacy: protecting data](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/privacy#Protecting-data).

## Widget: Household pickups

Configuration: choose a household and explicitly enable “Share pickup summary,” with explanation “Everyone viewing the shared face can see pickup counts and status.” Default shared publication is off. Select only parcels authorized for this household; private parcels do not contribute to counts. No shared configuration may enable recipient names, address, codes or item descriptions. A member’s personalized HomeView Home Screen remains distinct from the single shared Modular face; this product deliberately uses the same safe summary on both.

| Surface / family | Content in priority order | Activation |
|---|---|---|
| iPhone Home Screen / system small | “Household pickups”; large “1 ready” only after verified readiness; freshness line | Open selected household pickup list |
| HomeView Modular / system small | Same summary; larger count/status, removable background, no secondary controls | Open safe household pickup summary in the supported app context; private detail requires personal authenticated continuation |
| iPhone Lock Screen / accessory rectangular | “Pickups · 1 ready”; “Updated 2 min ago” | Open household pickup list after system access requirements |
| iPhone Lock Screen / accessory inline | “Pickups: 1 ready” when fresh; “Pickups: update needed” when stale | One target to the same pickup list; no simulated buttons |
| Optional watch glance / accessory rectangular in Smart Stack | “Pickups”; count/status; short freshness line | Corresponding pickup list in a watch app if supplied; defer this widget variant until that destination exists |

No watch-face complication is proposed; a future face placement requires its own Complications route. The delivery Live Activity can already provide a paired-watch Smart Stack glance as specified below. Supported family/context decisions come from [Widgets: anatomy and platform considerations](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/widgets#Anatomy); watch responsibility follows [Designing for watchOS](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/designing-for-watchos#Best-practices).

**Concrete supplied-data rendering:** no pickup readiness is known. Show:

> Household pickups  
> Status unavailable  
> Last update 35 min ago

If an actual prior snapshot contains a ready count, stale rendering instead reads “Last known: 1 ready” and “Updated 35 min ago · Check in app.” Never manufacture that count from the supplied parcel. At the largest text size, retain “Update needed” and the single app destination before optional headings or decoration.

Fresh ready example: “Household pickups / 1 ready / Updated 2 min ago.” Verified empty example: “No pickups ready / Updated 2 min ago”; unavailable data must never become a zero count. Gallery description: “Check household pickups.” Gallery previews use labeled simulated safe data, including the stale variant. Initial placeholder retains the title with placeholder blocks; prolonged absence becomes “Pickup status unavailable.”

## Freshness and connectivity contract

The following thresholds are **product decisions**, not Apple requirements: pickup data becomes stale after 15 minutes; active-delivery data after 5 minutes, or earlier when the server’s validity ends. Store source timestamp separately from fetch timestamp. A cache read or failed refresh never resets source age. Reject older event revisions; reject implausible future timestamps as unavailable until reconciled.

| Condition | Widget | Live Activity | Recovery |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fresh valid data | Verified count/status and source age | Verified stage and valid arrival window | Apply newer authoritative revisions only |
| Refresh in progress | Keep last known content and original age | Keep current content while validity holds | No blanking or fake progress |
| Stale, connection unknown | “Last known…” plus age; inline “Update needed” | “Update delayed”; last confirmed stage and age; hide ETA | Request update when allowed; open exact app context |
| Connection failure actually observed | “Offline · Last update 35 min ago” with last known state if any | “Offline · Update delayed”; source age; no ETA | App offers Retry; restore freshness only after successful authoritative update |
| No usable cached data | “Pickup status unavailable” | “Delivery status unavailable” | Open app; explain failure and retry there |
| Signed out / revoked membership | “Open app to set up pickups”; clear household cache | End associated activity and remove private local event association | Authenticate and recheck authorization; never reveal cached household data |
| Sharing disabled / no household selected | “Choose a household in the app”; no counts | No effect on separately authorized personal delivery | Explicit setup in app |

Age alone does not prove offline. With the supplied 35-minute update and no connectivity evidence, use **stale**, not “Offline.” Retain the last successful snapshot during errors. Schedule a stale-state timeline entry at expiry and request reloads on meaningful server changes; actual widget execution is system-controlled. Always show source age or “Last known” where delayed reload could otherwise imply freshness. System date presentation may update the age without network polling. On app entry, revalidate and expose Retry if needed. See [Widgets: updating content](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/widgets#Updating-widget-content).

## Private bounded delivery Live Activity

Start from the authenticated delivery detail when the person chooses “Follow delivery,” once an active event is confirmed; explain that safe delivery status can appear on the Lock Screen and paired displays. Respect unavailable/disabled system capability with the same status in the app. Provide “Stop following” in delivery detail; this ends tracking without cancelling the delivery. Do not start from the 35-minute-old snapshot alone.

Event data: opaque delivery ID, monotonic revision, confirmed stage, source timestamp, validity deadline, optional arrival window, event start, and planned monitoring end. Shared pickup publication uses a separate authorization and sanitized model. Do not collect location, contacts, camera, microphone or HomeKit access for these glances; logistics status comes from existing authorized service data.

**Lifecycle:** not followed → confirmed active → followed → delivered / cancelled / failed / monitoring expired → ended. Freshness is an independent state while followed. Example confirmed stages are “Preparing,” “On the way,” and “Arriving”; they change only on server evidence. Do not draw an elapsed-time percentage as physical delivery progress. The supplied 80 minutes is the planned event duration, not an arrival guarantee. At start + 80 minutes without terminal confirmation, end with “Tracking window ended · Open app for latest status,” never “Delivered.” A new bounded follow session requires a new confirmed event window and explicit user action.

On confirmed delivery, cancellation or failure, end immediately. Keep a safe terminal Lock Screen summary for 15 minutes, then remove it; Dynamic Island and CarPlay remove the ended activity immediately. Stop following, sign-out and access revocation request immediate removal without retained summary. Request termination through server and local paths as available; expiry/ending while offline must be verified against actual SDK/runtime support and must not rely on app foreground execution. The UI must still mark updates stale if an end signal is delayed. Apple recommends clearly bounded activities, ideally no more than 8 hours, with immediate ending and a shorter useful retained summary; 80 minutes fits that design guidance. See [Live Activities: lifecycle](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/live-activities#Starting-updating-and-ending-a-Live-Activity).

| Presentation | Fresh example (simulated) | Stale/offline replacement |
|---|---|---|
| Compact Dynamic Island | Leading parcel + stage symbol; trailing “12–20m” only with valid server ETA | Leading parcel + warning symbol; trailing “Stale” or “Offline”; omit stage if needed for fit |
| Minimal, including multiple activities | Parcel + stage/check/warning glyph conveying current state, rather than logo alone | Parcel + warning; accessible description includes update delay |
| Expanded | Top leading parcel + “Delivery”; top trailing valid arrival window; below confirmed stage and source age | Same identity positions; “Update delayed” or “Offline”; “Last confirmed: On the way”; “Updated 35 min ago”; omit arrival window |
| Lock Screen | “Delivery”; prominent confirmed stage; valid arrival window; source age; one “Details” link | “Delivery / Update delayed / Updated 35 min ago / Details”; add last known stage only when known |

All taps, including both compact halves, resolve the opaque delivery ID to the same authenticated delivery detail, preserving context through interruption and sign-in. “Details” is the only action; Accept and Cancel remain inside authenticated detail after current-state validation. No cancellation or acceptance is queued silently while offline. Multiple deliveries retain independent opaque IDs; minimal presentations remain distinguishable by accessible event labels without exposing recipient/address.

Updates occur only for changed content, validity or lifecycle; no one-second polling, fake live spinner, or speculative countdown to delivery. Alert once for a confirmed crucial arrival/action-needed event, subject to user/system settings; do not issue a duplicate push. Staleness alone is a quiet status change. [Live Activities: presentation and interactivity](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/live-activities#Presentation).

## Appearance, privacy and continuation

Use semantic system text styles: headline for status, body for detail, caption for freshness, medium/semibold for essential Live Activity text. Use actual text and scalable symbols. Stack source age beneath status, remove optional heading/detail before essential state, and grow expanded/Lock Screen content within system constraints. Keep fixed-family widget layouts flexible instead of assuming one production canvas. Preserve core stale/unknown wording through long text, Bold Text and large text. [Typography: Dynamic Type](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/typography#Supporting-Dynamic-Type).

Full color: semantic foreground/background. Accented: primary group holds state and freshness; accent group holds only supporting parcel identity. Vibrant: opaque grayscale values preserve hierarchy. Test light/dark, tinted/clear and removed backgrounds. HomeView Modular and StandBy use background removal and readable large summaries; red monochrome Night Mode retains written stale state. Do not use color alone for ready/offline/stale. Only Lock Screen Live Activity gets a restrained custom background; Dynamic Island backgrounds remain system-owned. See [Widgets: rendering modes](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/widgets#Rendering-modes) and [Live Activities: colors](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/live-activities#Choosing-colors).

Always On pairs: active shows status, freshness and Details; dimmed preserves positions and safe status, reduces secondary emphasis, and does not animate. No names, address or code appear in either. Resume preserves selected event. Respect system privacy redaction, using “Delivery update / Open app for details” if needed. Always On support depends on hardware/OS; the local guide’s specific device examples are not a complete current support list. [Always On](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/always-on#Best-practices).

Paired watch Live Activity: use default Smart Stack composition with stage/valid arrival window or “Update delayed”; tap opens watch detail if available, otherwise system full-screen continuation with paired-iPhone launch. No independent watch app is assumed. StandBy uses the safe Lock Screen layout scaled for distance and red-mode legibility. CarPlay shows readable status without depending on buttons/toggles, which are disabled there. Paired Mac activation follows system iPhone Mirroring. Do not promise Live Activity support on HomeView, tvOS or visionOS from this guide; HomeView receives the summary widget. [Live Activities: destination qualifications](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/live-activities#Platform-considerations).

Privacy data-purpose matrix:

| Data | Purpose / location | Access policy |
|---|---|---|
| Household authorized pickup count and timestamp | Shared glance, sanitized widget cache | Explicit sharing selection; exclude private parcels; purge on revocation |
| Delivery stage, timestamp, valid arrival window | Personal bounded activity | Followed event only; safe even when externally visible |
| Recipient and street address | Identify destination in app | Authenticated authorized detail only |
| Gate code | Entry instruction in app | Authenticated explicit reveal; encrypted secret storage where cached; never surface payload or URL |

This minimizes exposure; it does not certify security. Shared caches and already-rendered snapshots may persist until system refresh/removal. Revocation propagation and secure cache deletion require implementation evidence. [Privacy: best practices](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/privacy#Best-practices).

Choose size, location, and rendering behavior together. ## Anatomy WidgetKit supplies contextual treatment, but tailor the layout when a context needs a better information hierarchy. ### System family widgets Small commonly focuses on one fact, medium/large on more information/actions, extra large adds room where supported, and extra-large portrait is spatial-only. Rendering mode varies by context rather than following one universal rule. |Platform |Full-color |Accented |Vibrant | |----------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------| |iPhone |Home Screen, Today view, StandBy and CarPlay (with the background removed)|Home Screen and Today view |Lock Screen, StandBy in Night Mode| |iPad |Home Screen and Today view |Home Screen and Today view |Lock Screen | |Apple Watch |Smart Stack, complications |Smart Stack, complications |Not supported | |Mac |Desktop and Notification Center |Not supported |Desktop | |Apple Vision Pro|Horizontal and vertical surfaces |Horizontal and vertical surfaces |Not supported | |Apple HomeView |Home Screen, Modular face (with the background removed) |Home Screen, Modular face (with the background removed)|Modular face in Night Mode | ## Best practices Choose a simple purpose central to the app and useful changing information. A static app-icon replica offers little benefit. Use multiple sizes only when they add layers of useful information, not stretched copies. Balance immediate clarity with secondary details available on longer inspection. Keep larger variants on the same core purpose. Brand through restrained color/type/glyphs; if source attribution needs a logo, a small upper-trailing mark suffices. Offer configuration when people must choose their content; otherwise useful automatic recents can remove setup. Avoid lookalike widget elements inside the app that behave differently. Explain any signed-in functionality when logged out. A subtle occasion-specific visual treatment can add delight without losing utility. ### Updating widget content Widgets refresh periodically under system limits rather than continuously. Match updates to meaningful changes and expected viewing, adding freshness text when data can age between checks. Use system date/time views to preserve reload budget. Show available data promptly instead of replacing it with placeholders while refreshing. Standard/custom transitions of up to 2 seconds can reveal new data. ### Adding interactivity Ordinary widget activation opens the app; native buttons/toggles can do simple relevant work in place. Deep-link precisely to the selected content. Keep targets clear and glanceable instead of recreating a miniature app. Inline accessories have one tap target. ### Choosing margins and padding Supply adaptable content and let system sizing handle device scale; iPad can render a larger canvas before downscaling. Most widgets use 16-pt margins; 11 pt can suit tighter grouped graphics/buttons/background shapes. Mac desktop and Lock Screen/StandBy use smaller contextual margins. Use container-relative rounding so inset shapes align with the outer corners. ### Displaying text in widgets Prefer system text styles and aligned SF Symbols. Custom type should be sparse and readable, often limited to large text with SF Pro for small labels. Generally keep type at least 11 pt. Render actual text rather than rasterizing so scaling and VoiceOver work. In iOS, iPadOS, and visionOS, SwiftUI system/custom fonts support Dynamic Type Large through AX5. ### Using color Use color to support content rather than compete with it, and provide noncolor meaning because tinting, grayscale, and watch-face inversion can change the result. Widget editing colors can come from the asset catalog. Preserving full-color images in clear/tinted modes can overpower system customization; reserve it for meaningful media such as artwork and keep images smaller than the whole widget where appropriate. ## Rendering modes ### Full-color Support light/dark through semantic colors or asset variants, normally matching light backgrounds to light appearance and dark to dark. ### Accented Separate primary and accent groups. The system applies context-dependent solid colors; watch uses white for primary and the selected watch-face color for accent. Preserve hierarchy across all tint/clear options. The source's platform table excludes accented Mac mode while one prose sentence mentions Mac group tinting; do not infer Mac support from that conflicting sentence. ### Vibrant Pixel opacity controls how much background material passes through, while grayscale brightness determines visual emphasis. Use opaque white/light gray for prominent information and darker opaque grays for supporting details. Check grayscale contrast; varying white opacity is not a substitute for optimized grayscale values. ## Previews and placeholders Gallery previews should show realistic real or simulated data promptly and accurately represent each variant. Loading placeholders can preserve static framing and use semitransparent blocks for dynamic text or images. Describe the widget with an approachable sentence-case action verb, omitting filler about adding/using a widget. Group its sizes under one description. The gallery Add button can use an appropriate brand color. ## Platform considerations No additional macOS rules are specified. Widgets are unsupported in tvOS. ### iOS, iPadOS Treat Lock Screen widgets like complications: useful data first, with inline above the clock and circular/rectangular below. Verify reduced-luminance Always On grayscale. For frequent real-time bounded updates, design a Live Activity, reusing appropriate components rather than expecting widget refreshes to behave continuously. #### StandBy and CarPlay StandBy shows two scaled small-family widgets; CarPlay also scales that family with removable backgrounds. Use large readable information and restrained rich imagery, especially for across-room or driving glances. Mark backgrounds removable. Test red monochrome in low-light StandBy. #### Apple HomeView Small-family widgets can appear on a shared Modular face and personalized Home Screens, sourced locally or from connected household iPhones/iPads. The household has one Modular face with up to four widgets, potentially exposing one person's calendar to others. Each enrolled member has their own Home Screen; consider the privacy difference. ### visionOS Widgets persist on horizontal/vertical surfaces through device restarts at consistent real-world scale. Full color is default; selected palette tints use accented mode. Elevated frames have customizable widths, and widget-specific themes can exist despite no global light/dark appearance. Design as room objects, from desk information to wall posters, and test all palettes and lighting, including elements excluded from tinting. #### Thresholds and sizes Design nearby/default and distant/simplified versions. At a distance, enlarge type, reduce detail, and remove controls; retain common elements across thresholds for continuity. Match family size to the likely surface. People can scale to 75–125%, so use clear hierarchy and high-resolution assets readable across distances. #### Mounting styles Elevated is default and works on walls and horizontal surfaces, tilting back on desks and casting a grounding shadow. Recessed sets content into vertical surfaces only, suitable for ambient/windowlike content. Opt out of unsuitable styles; recessed-only widgets cannot be placed horizontally. Mounting support applies per configuration, so separate configurations when variants need different support. Test every elevated frame width because layout cannot adapt to the selected frame. #### Treatment styles Paper provides a solid print-like object whose whole appearance follows ambient brightness. Glass separates foreground and background: important foreground stays bright/full color while supporting material adapts to lighting. Choose paper for artwork/posters and glass for information needing reliable contrast. ### watchOS Smart Stack backgrounds default black; a meaningful custom color can communicate state. Supply relevance based on location or current system activity to encourage timely display/placement. ## Specifications Use these factual dimensions as design guidance and keep production layouts flexible. # Live Activities Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/live-activities) Snapshot: 2026-10-25. Original implementation guidance derived from the source. ## Contents - [Anatomy](#Anatomy) - [Best practices](#Best-practices) - [Presentation](#Presentation) - [CarPlay](#CarPlay) - [Platform considerations](#Platform-considerations) - [Specifications](#Specifications) Live Activities track a bounded task or event through frequent updates over a few hours. They begin on iPhone or iPad and can appear on the Lock/Home Screen, Dynamic Island and StandBy, paired Mac menu bar, Apple Watch Smart Stack, and CarPlay Dashboard. ## Anatomy Support compact, minimal, expanded, and Lock Screen presentations. The system composes these for available space and devices. ### Compact A single Dynamic Island activity uses separate leading/trailing elements around the TrueDepth camera. ### Minimal Multiple activities use compact circular/oval treatments, up to three where supported: one attached and others detached. Tap opens the app; hold expands. ### Expanded Holding compact/minimal content reveals a larger presentation. ### Lock Screen A bottom banner uses a layout related to expanded. On devices without Dynamic Island, essential update alerts can briefly overlay this banner on Home or another app. ### StandBy Minimal content expands on tap to a Lock Screen layout scaled 2×. A custom background extends across the screen. ## Best practices Use tasks with clear starts and ends, ideally no more than 8 hours. Show only immediately useful information, with details in the app. Exclude ads and promotions. Avoid exposed sensitive content; summarize or redact and offer app access/configuration. Match app identity across appearances; a logo mark can appear without a container, but do not use the full app icon. Do not draw attention to Dynamic Island from inside the app. Use legible large text, generally medium weight or stronger. ### Creating Live Activity layouts Adapt to actual screens and scale factors. Keep layout only as large as content needs. For limited-width Dynamic Island contexts, fit compact/minimal content within a 28-pt circle with abbreviations or graphics; use leading-only when a meaningful trailing version cannot fit. Favor familiar templates, even concentric margins, and container-relative corner radii. Inset groups or use a thick dividing line instead of extending content to edges. A blurred drawing-tool preview can help align angular content within rounded corners. Adjust Lock Screen/expanded height as available information grows or shrinks. ### Choosing colors Only Lock Screen permits custom background colors; compact, minimal, and expanded backgrounds are system-controlled. Dynamic Island is opaque black, so meaningful bold foreground color can express identity. Match its dark-background keyline to related content. Check custom Lock Screen contrast in both appearances and reduced-luminance Always On. ### Adding transitions and animating content updates Animations can last at most 2 seconds and are not played in reduced-luminance Always On. Use numeric changes, fades, scale, or movement to explain updates. Preserve existing elements as layout grows rather than removing/readding everything. Avoid transition collisions; animate a moved item and fade other list elements when needed. ### Offering interactivity Deep-link to the relevant task. Favor one essential button or toggle for a direct action, pause/resume, or response to meaningful progress, preserving space for status and reducing accidental activation. ### Starting, updating, and ending a Live Activity Begin at expected moments, including automatic starts for followed events, with an easy opt-out in the corresponding app view. Offer an App Shortcut when useful. Update only for changed content. Alert only for crucial updates and avoid a parallel push for the same information. Prefer one dynamically changing activity for related simultaneous events. End immediately when the task ends: Dynamic Island/CarPlay remove it, while Lock Screen, Mac, and watch can retain it for up to 4 hours. Choose a shorter useful summary lifetime, commonly 15–30 minutes, proportional to the activity. ## Presentation Design the iPhone presentations first, then tailor layouts for StandBy, watch, and driving while supporting every destination. ### Compact presentation Show essential changing data. Make both halves read as one through coherent color/type and balanced widths. Fit snugly against the camera without extra inner padding or unnecessary status-bar obstruction; shorten units or precision as needed. Both halves should deep-link to the same relevant app screen. ### Minimal presentation Preserve recognition while conveying current information instead of only a static logo. ### Expanded presentation Expand predictably from the smaller layout, retaining relative positions and fitting content close to the camera rather than leaving unused gaps. ### Lock Screen presentation Create a distinct task layout rather than copying notification structure. Use restrained tint/background customization to fit personalized wallpapers. Verify contrast in both appearances and Always On, including the system-generated dismiss-button color; override its foreground if needed. Standard margins are 14 pt, with tighter spacing only when content grouping needs it. ### StandBy presentation Supply assets and, where useful, a custom layout for the larger scale. The default background blends with the bezel and surroundings and permits slightly more content scale. Preserve margins so expansion does not crop graphics, and test the red-tinted Night Mode. ## CarPlay The default combines compact halves. A supplemental small family can support larger type and more information. Its custom layout is also used on watch, but CarPlay disables buttons and toggles; driving-oriented activities should prioritize timely content over those controls. ## Platform considerations No additional iOS or iPadOS rules are specified. Live Activities are unsupported in tvOS and visionOS. ### macOS Paired Mac menu-bar presentations use compact/minimal/expanded styles. Activation opens the app through iPhone Mirroring. ### watchOS The activity appears atop the paired watch's Smart Stack, combining compact halves by default. Tap opens a watch app when available; otherwise it opens a full-screen view with a paired-iPhone launch button. A custom layout can improve essential progress, changes, and controls, but consider its shared use in CarPlay where interaction is disabled. ## Specifications These source dimensions are design guidance in points; Evaluate actual support before describing Accessibility Nutrition Labels on the App Store. ## Vision Support text enlargement of at least 200%; the source gives 140% for watchOS. Dynamic Type or equivalent custom resizing must preserve usability. Follow platform defaults/minima when choosing custom styles, and enlarge thin-weight custom fonts further when needed. |Platform|Default text|Minimum text| |---|---:|---:| |iOS, iPadOS|17 pt|11 pt| |macOS|13 pt|10 pt| |tvOS|29 pt|23 pt| |visionOS|17 pt|12 pt| |watchOS|16 pt|12 pt| Measure contrast using established calculators such as WCAG or APCA. Apple’s Accessibility Inspector table uses these WCAG-AA guidance values: text up to 17 pt, all weights, 4.5:1; 18 pt at all weights, 3:1; bold text at any size, 3:1. Preserve the table’s stated scope rather than assuming it replaces a separate conformance evaluation. If default colors fall short, Increase Contrast must supply a higher-contrast scheme. Test both light and dark. Prefer semantic system colors that adapt to accessibility preferences. Pair color with shape, icons, or text; red/green and blue/orange distinctions can be difficult. Let people customize chart or character colors where useful. Give VoiceOver meaningful descriptions of interface and content. ## Hearing Make dialogue and important information available without sound. Captions describe audible information in synchrony with media, subtitles present dialogue in a chosen language, audio descriptions narrate otherwise visual events in audio pauses, and transcripts provide a complete text account of audible and visual information. Let people adjust text presentation. Pair sound feedback with matching haptics and visual direction cues, especially for offscreen game or spatial events. Music Haptics and audio graphs on iOS/iPadOS can offer tactile representations of music and data. ## Mobility Use comfortable controls and sufficient separation, not just adequate visible size. |Platform|Default control|Minimum control| |---|---:|---:| |iOS, iPadOS|44 × 44 pt|28 × 28 pt| |macOS|28 × 28 pt|20 × 20 pt| |tvOS|66 × 66 pt|56 × 56 pt| |visionOS|60 × 60 pt|28 × 28 pt| |watchOS|44 × 44 pt|28 × 28 pt| The source suggests around 12 pt padding for bezelled elements and 24 pt outside visible edges for elements without a bezel. Use simple gestures for repeated tasks and offer an onscreen alternative for essential gestures, such as a dismiss button alongside swipe-to-dismiss. Avoid requiring complex multiple-finger or multiple-hand actions. Label controls so Voice Control can target them. Siri/Shortcuts can expose repeated tasks through voice, Action buttons, Home Screen, and Control Center. Test VoiceOver, AssistiveTouch, Full Keyboard Access, Pointer Control, and Switch Control rather than assuming support. ## Speech Support complete keyboard navigation and Full Keyboard Access; preserve system accessibility shortcuts. Support Switch Control navigation and activation through hardware, controller, and sound inputs such as a click or pop, so speech is never a necessary input method. ## Cognitive Use familiar, simple, consistent navigation and gestures. Prefer explicit dismissal over timed disappearance, allowing time for processing and assistive navigation. Games can offer difficulty, reaction-time, success-criteria, and control-assistance accommodations. Give clear playback controls and consider a global autoplay preference. Respect Dim Flashing Lights during media playback. Honor Reduce Motion by reducing automatic and repeated movement, scaling, zooming, and peripheral effects. Reduce spring bounce; tie appropriate motion directly to gestures; avoid animated depth changes and blur transitions; replace spatial translations with fades. Fast or blinking motion can distract, cause dizziness, or trigger seizures. For Assistive Access on iOS/iPadOS, focus on core tasks, remove nonessential workflows, and split multistep tasks into one interaction per screen. The source requires two confirmations for actions that are difficult to reverse, such as deletion, in this mode. ## Platform considerations The source adds no separate rules for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, tvOS, or watchOS beyond the guidance above. ### visionOS Support hand/head Pointer Control and Zoom. Keep controls inside a comfortable field of view; horizontal arrangements usually strain the neck less than tall ones. Avoid rapid shifts of attention among distant locations. Reduce peripheral animation speed and intensity, use gentle camera/video motion, and avoid making the surrounding world move without the person’s control. Do not lock content to the head, which can feel confining and interfere with Pointer Control. Minimize large or repeated gestures and consider the physical surroundings. ## Resources Consult the [official article](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/accessibility) for linked Apple design assets and implementation resources. #### Related The official article links the adjacent HIG topics relevant to this guidance. #### Developer documentation Use the framework references linked by Apple for current API availability and implementation details. #### Videos Apple’s linked design sessions provide demonstrations and additional implementation context; no video review is implied here. ## Change log Source revision dates: June 9, 2025, March 7, 2025, June 10, 2024, December 5, 2023, June 21, 2023.

# Privacy Source: [Apple Human Interface Guidelines](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/privacy) · Retrieved 2026-10-25. This is original application guidance based on the source text. Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. Communicate collection and usage clearly and protect granted data. Keep App Store privacy disclosures accurate for new releases and updates; people rely on them before downloading. ## Best practices Collect only what the specific feature requires and make access as precise as possible. Respect Hide My Email, Mail Privacy Protection, and tracking choices. Prefer on-device processing, including Create ML/Neural Engine where useful, to avoid unnecessary server transfers. Use system encryption, key management, and established security protections, including CloudKit’s additional encrypted data types where available. ## Requesting permission Protected categories include personal/location/health/financial/contact information, user-created content, messages/calendar/music/gameplay/HomeKit data, media, Bluetooth/Wi-Fi/local network resources, camera/microphone, the advertising identifier, and permission-gated ARKit data in a visionOS Full Space. The system displays the app’s purpose string and stores choices/descriptions in privacy settings. Ask when the person invokes the relevant feature. Request at launch only when access is essential and obviously necessary, such as location for navigation or room information for a spatial game that needs walls. Write a short, specific, active, complete sentence in sentence case with a period, explaining both use and reason. Vague promises of a better experience and commands to enable access do not explain the need. ### Pre-alert screens, windows, or views Usually context explains the request. If extra explanation is essential, use one button clearly leading to the system alert, such as Continue/Next; do not label it Allow or mimic the actual consent choice. Do not add cancellation, close, or other actions except those needed for legal consent. These restrictions apply to pre-permission custom explanations, not ordinary unrelated onboarding screens. ### Tracking requests Show the AppTrackingTransparency alert before collecting tracking information, including if tracking begins at launch. Do not offer incentives, imitate a permission prompt, display an image of the alert, annotate behind it, or otherwise manipulate rushed choices. Such patterns can cause App Review rejection. A legally required consent view before/after the system alert is permitted by the source’s stated review guidance. ## Location button On iOS/iPadOS/watchOS, the system location button provides one-time access at the task’s moment of need. The first tap teaches and confirms its behavior through a system alert; later taps grant access without repeating that education. Authorization expires when app use ends. With no prior status it resembles Allow Once; an existing While Using status is unchanged. Use it for individual tasks such as attaching a location or finding a nearby item/store. Customize only the supplied title, filled/outline glyph, foreground/background colors, and corner radius. Keep all localized and accessibility-size text untruncated and maintain contrast/transparency limits. Persistent customization violations can prevent location access even though the button still triggers other app actions. ## Protecting data Prefer passkeys; if passwords remain, add two-factor verification. Use Face ID, Optic ID, or Touch ID to protect continued signed-in access where appropriate. Store secrets in the encrypted keychain, never plaintext files even with restrictive permissions. Prefer established authentication, Sign in with Apple, and Password AutoFill over invented schemes. ## Platform considerations No extra iOS/iPadOS/tvOS/watchOS rules are listed. ### macOS Sign externally distributed apps with a valid Developer ID. Use sandboxing to limit resource/data access; Mac App Store apps require it. Account for fast user switching rather than assuming the current person is the only signed-in account. ### visionOS System ARKit algorithms support lighting, mapping, persistence, segmentation, and related rendering in Shared Space without exposing raw data to apps. ARKit API access requires Full Space, and plane estimation, scene reconstruction, image anchoring, and hand tracking require permission. Gaze remains private: system hover feedback can respond before a tap without disclosing where someone looks. Compatibility back-camera input is blank; front-camera input represents spatial Personas with permission. Adapt imported phone/tablet camera-dependent features by removal or content import instead of assuming conventional camera capture. ## Resources Consult the [official article](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/privacy) for linked Apple design assets and implementation resources. #### Related The official article links the adjacent HIG topics relevant to this guidance. #### Developer documentation Use the framework references linked by Apple for current API availability and implementation details. #### Videos Apple’s linked design sessions provide demonstrations and additional implementation context; no video review is implied here. ## Change log Source revision dates: June 21, 2023.

Independent media review is recorded separately in the coverage report. ## Contents - [Ensuring legibility](#Ensuring-legibility) - [Conveying hierarchy](#Conveying-hierarchy) - [Using system fonts](#Using-system-fonts) - [Using custom fonts](#Using-custom-fonts) - [Supporting Dynamic Type](#Supporting-Dynamic-Type) - [Platform considerations](#Platform-considerations) - [Specifications](#Specifications) - [Resources](#Resources) - [Change log](#Change-log) ## Ensuring legibility Test type at real viewing distances, lighting conditions, and supported devices. Enlarge hard-to-read text, improve foreground/background contrast, or choose a more legible face. Prefer Regular, Medium, Semibold, or Bold over Ultralight/Thin/Light, especially at small sizes. Thin custom faces often need sizes above the recommendations. |Platform|Default|Minimum| |---|---:|---:| |iOS, iPadOS|17 pt|11 pt| |macOS|13 pt|10 pt| |tvOS|29 pt|23 pt| |visionOS|17 pt|12 pt| |watchOS|16 pt|12 pt| ## Conveying hierarchy Combine size, weight, and color to distinguish levels, and preserve those relationships as text grows. Limit typeface families so differences retain meaning. Prioritize content people intend to read when scaling: body/dialogue may need growth while tab labels or transient damage numbers need not grow equally. ## Using system fonts San Francisco includes Pro, Compact, Arabic, Armenian, Georgian, Hebrew, and Mono variants; all listed except Mono also have rounded alternatives. New York is a complementary serif family. Variable fonts interpolate weights and optical design continuously for the exact point size, rather than requiring separate Text/Display font choices except in limited design tools. SF offers widths such as Condensed/Expanded and weights from Ultralight through Black; equivalent SF Symbol weights enable precise matching. Use semantic text styles to express hierarchy through coordinated weight, size, and leading, and to inherit Dynamic Type/accessibility adjustments where supported. Modify symbolic traits for emphasis or line spacing when justified. Loose leading supports long passages or wide columns; tight leading can fit constrained rows, but avoid it for three or more lines. Access system fonts through platform APIs (`default`, `serif`, and the font-design constants), without embedding the files. Runtime tracking adapts by size automatically; mockups may need the tracking values below. ## Using custom fonts Check custom faces against platform size recommendations and actual conditions. Implement Dynamic Type and Bold Text behavior equivalent to the system faces. Apple’s Unity accessibility plug-in can support Dynamic Type in games; if unsuitable, offer a separate text-size adjustment. ## Supporting Dynamic Type Dynamic Type is available in iOS, iPadOS, tvOS, visionOS, and watchOS. Test every supported size, including Larger Accessibility Text on iPhone/iPad. Scale meaningful glyphs as well as text; SF Symbols integrate automatically. Preserve useful information at the largest accessibility size rather than aggressively truncating. Give labels enough lines and avoid truncation in scrolling regions unless a detail view exposes the full text. Stack inline timestamps/glyphs beneath or above primary text, grow containers, and reduce columns when width becomes cramped.
